title: Finite families of constant set-sheaf sections lift on a common cover
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $U$ an etale object [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and $J$ either its small etale topology or its localization at $U$. Let $S$ be any set, $T$ an object of this site, $I$ a finite set, and $z_i$ sections over $T$ of the constant set sheaf at $S$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Write $\eta_W:S\to\underline S(W)$ for the sheafification unit [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. (1) There exists a covering sieve $R$ of $T$ such that, for every arrow $g:W\to T$ in $R$ and every $i\in I$, there exists $s\in S$ with $\eta_W(s)=z_i|_W$. (2) If the empty sieve does not cover $W$, the function $\eta_W$ is injective. The first assertion does not require $S$ itself finite.

proof.text: For (1), specialize the proved finite-family lifting theorem in ConstantSheafSections to Type-valued sheaves and the given localized etale site. Its proof intersects the finitely many covering image sieves. For (2), specialize the proved injectivity theorem to the same topology. It uses local injectivity of the unit and the identity restriction maps of the constant presheaf.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $J$ be a Grothendieck topology on a category $\mathcal C$ and let $\mathcal A$ be a concrete category admitting sheafification for $J$ in which a morphism of presheaves becomes an isomorphism after sheafification exactly when it is locally injective and locally surjective (for instance sets or modules over a ring). Let $N$ be an object of $\mathcal A$, let $\underline N$ be the sheafification of the constant presheaf with value $N$, and write $\eta_V:N\to\underline N(V)$ for the component at $V$ of the sheafification map.
(1) Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal C$, $I$ a finite set and $z_i\in\underline N(U)$ for $i\in I$. There is a covering sieve $R$ of $U$ such that for every arrow $g:V\to U$ in $R$ and every $i\in I$ there is $n\in N$ with $\eta_V(n)=z_i|_V$.
(2) If $U$ is an object of $\mathcal C$ which is not covered by the empty sieve, then $\eta_U:N\to\underline N(U)$ is injective.
No finiteness of $N$ is required.

proof.text: Since the sheafification map of the constant presheaf is locally surjective, every section $z_i$ has a covering image sieve: the sieve of arrows $g:V\to U$ for which $z_i|_V$ lies in the image of $\eta_V$. A finite intersection of covering sieves is covering, so the intersection $R$ of these finitely many image sieves proves (1).

For (2), let $n,n'\in N$ with $\eta_U(n)=\eta_U(n')$. Since the sheafification map is locally injective, the sieve of arrows $g:V\to U$ on which the restrictions of $n$ and $n'$ in the constant presheaf agree is covering. The restriction maps of the constant presheaf are identities, so if $n\neq n'$ this sieve is the empty sieve, which by hypothesis does not cover $U$. Hence $n=n'$.
